hook.text: In the 1800s, milk killed thousands of children every year. Tuberculosis, typhoid, and diphtheria lurked inside.

buildup.text: Raw milk from urban dairies was a breeding ground for bacteria. Cows lived in filthy conditions.

discovery.text: Louis Pasteur showed that heating milk to 72°C for 15 seconds killed dangerous pathogens without ruining taste.

twist.text: Dairy companies fought pasteurization for decades—it cost money and they preferred blaming consumers.

climax.text: Mandatory pasteurization became law in most countries by mid-1900s. Child milk-borne deaths plummeted.

punchline.text: Heating milk for 15 seconds saved millions of lives.

quiz.question: What does pasteurization do to milk?
options: Heats it briefly to kill dangerous pathogens

details.summary: Pasteurization heats milk to kill harmful bacteria, making it safe for consumption and extending shelf life. This topic covers Louis Pasteur's discovery, how pasteurization transformed the dairy industry, and the ongoing raw milk debate.
details.whyItMatters: Before pasteurization, milk-borne diseases killed thousands annually. This single process made dairy products safe for mass consumption and enabled the modern dairy supply chain.
takeaways: Pasteurization heats milk to 72°C for 15 seconds to kill harmful bacteria
It reduced milk-borne illness deaths by over 90% when widely adopted
Raw milk advocates argue pasteurization destroys beneficial enzymes and bacteria

faq.question: What does pasteurization do to milk?
faq.answer: Standard pasteurization (HTST) heats milk to 72°C for 15 seconds, killing pathogenic bacteria like Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria while preserving most nutritional value. Ultra-pasteurization (UHT) heats to 135°C for 2 seconds for shelf-stable milk.

faq.question: Is raw milk safe to drink?
faq.answer: Health authorities in most countries advise against raw milk consumption due to risks of bacterial contamination. While raw milk advocates cite taste and probiotic benefits, the CDC attributes thousands of foodborne illness cases annually to unpasteurized dairy.
